items.q: A business employed an average of 90 people during the year and 25 left. What is its labour turnover?
items.why: Labour turnover = number leaving ÷ average number employed × 100 = 25 ÷ 90 × 100 = 27.8%.
items.label: New question

items.q: Magpie plc (all figures £m): sales revenue 80, cost of sales 50, bank overdraft 7, inventory 8, payables 12, receivables 17. These are all its current assets and current liabilities, and inventory is the same as the average for the year. Calculate its current ratio.
items.why: Current assets = inventory £8m + receivables £17m = £25m. Current liabilities = overdraft £7m + payables £12m = £19m. Current ratio = 25 ÷ 19 = 1.32:1. The overdraft is a current liability.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2022 Q18

items.q: Output = 200 units, Selling price = £7.25, Fixed costs = £500, Contribution per unit = £3. The variable cost per unit is:
items.why: Contribution per unit = Selling price - Variable cost. So: 3 = 7.25 - VC. Therefore VC = 7.25 - 3 = £4.25. Contribution per unit is simply: Price - Variable Cost.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Magpie plc (all figures £m): sales revenue 80, cost of sales 50, bank overdraft 7, inventory 8, payables 12, receivables 17. These are all its current assets and current liabilities, and inventory is the same as the average for the year. Calculate its payables days.
items.why: Payables days = payables ÷ cost of sales × 365 = £12m ÷ £50m × 365 = 87.6 days.
items.label: Paper 1 June 2022 Q17

items.q: Fixed costs are £4,000, the selling price is £12 and variable costs are £8 per unit. The business currently sells 1,400 units. What is its margin of safety?
items.why: Break-even = £4,000 ÷ (£12 – £8) = 1,000 units. Margin of safety = actual output – break-even output = 1,400 – 1,000 = 400 units. The answer is in units, not pounds.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company has revenue of £264m, operating profit of £33m and capital employed of £170m. What is its return on capital employed (ROCE)?
items.label: New question

items.q: A product sells for £20. Variable cost per unit is £15 and fixed costs are £19,000. What is the break-even output?
items.why: Contribution per unit = price – variable cost = £20 – £15 = £5. Break-even output = fixed costs ÷ contribution per unit = £19,000 ÷ £5 = 3,800 units.
items.label: New question

items.q: The decision tree shows two options. Which option should be chosen on financial grounds, and what is its net gain?
items.why: Option A: expected value = (0.3 × £18m) + (0.7 × £5m) = £8.9m. Net gain = £8.9m – £8m = £0.9m. Option B: expected value = (0.25 × £9m) + (0.75 × £3m) = £4.5m. Net gain = £4.5m – £1m = £3.5m. Option B has the higher net gain. Compare net gains, not expected values.
items.label: New question

items.q: A company achieved a ROCE of 20% with capital employed of £100m. What was its operating profit?
items.why: ROCE = operating profit ÷ capital employed × 100, so operating profit = ROCE × capital employed = 20% × £100m = £20m.
items.label: New question

items.q: 120 employees, labour costs £2.7m. Costs increase 3%, employees stay same. Labour costs per employee in 2017?
items.why: New total costs = 2,700,000 x 1.03 = £2,781,000. Cost per employee = 2,781,000 / 120 = £23,175. Two-step calculation: first increase total costs by 3%, then divide by number of employees.
items.label: Past paper question
